title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 301 (Arrest of person trying to leave India or abscond)

content.overview: Where a winding-up order has been made, the Tribunal may, on the application of the Company Liquidator, order the arrest of a person who is about to quit India or to abscond, or to remove or conceal any of his property, for the purpose of evading examination, payment of monies, or production of books or papers.
content.glance: Tribunal may order arrest of a person about to leave India or abscond, or to remove/conceal property, to evade examination or payment in a winding-up.
content.study: Section 301 empowers the Tribunal, after a winding-up order, on the Company Liquidator's application, to order the arrest of a person who is about to leave India or abscond, or to remove or conceal property, in order to evade examination under the Act, payment of monies, or production of books or papers. The power is preservative.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: Winding-up order has been made; application by Company Liquidator.

sections.heading: Grounds
sections.body: Person is about to quit India or abscond, or to remove or conceal property, for the purpose of evading examination, payment, or production of books/papers.

sections.heading: Order
sections.body: Tribunal may order arrest; may also order seizure of books and property.

provisions.title: Arrest of person trying to leave India or abscond

examples.title: Absconding risk
examples.body: A director against whom the liquidator has reported fraud is about to leave the country. The liquidator may apply under s. 301 for an arrest order to secure examination.

hypotheticals.question: When may the Tribunal order arrest under s. 301?
hypotheticals.analysis: After a winding-up order, on the Company Liquidator's application, where the person is about to leave India or abscond, or to remove/conceal property, to evade examination, payment or production of books.

misconceptions.trap: Any creditor may apply for arrest under s. 301 without a liquidator application.
misconceptions.correction: Section 301 requires an application by the Company Liquidator after a winding-up order.
